questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was looking for a city and university that could provide a wide range of cinema courses and additional courses, which I would not have the opportunity to find at the University of Copenhagen. I ended up choosing Toronto because of the way the city centers cinematic events, and because of UofT's cinema program. Furthermore, Toronto is a diverse and multicultural city, which I wished to find as well during my exchange program. Toronto has a big city life, where different cultures meet, but is also surrounded by much beautiful nature. So it is easy to get all the good aspects of Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UofT was good at providing information upon arrival. The professors were good at handing out maps to find the classrooms, and if there were ever any questions, I could easily call someone and ask for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was provided with a mentor, who was either an exchange student who had been here since August/September or a Torontonian citizen- and UofT student. The mentor was connected to 5-6 exchange students and helped out with finding our way around the campus and how to access university facilities such as fitness and creativities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The whole orientation was good, but often updates were needed due to Covid.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to live in Toronto, but I stayed at Co-op Housing, which is by far the cheapest and most social place to live! I lived with 12 roommates in a house very close to campus, and everyone was from each their own country. A great opportunity to meet other people than exchange students and to meet people from all over the world.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You talk more with people who are not on exchange, which several exchange students look to find. However, it is often very expensive to live off campus, so unless you can get a spot in a co-op house, I would recommend living on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was tough getting courses because exchange students do not have the same access as normal UofT students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to fill in a Google Sheets document and apply for the courses you have an interest in. There will be three different rounds, where you can apply for courses and drop them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It is easy to contact the university for help. They usually answer within a couple of days. Also, check the 'timetable' for available courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get the courses I wished for at first, but the courses I ended up with were great! Many courses have a wide title and therefore, the professor chooses an overall theme for the course. I had a course called Special Topics in Cinema as a Social and Cultural Practice, which ended up being a course in Film Festivals. It was so great, and not a course you would find in DK. In the end, I could not picture having other courses than the ones I had, and I would not have changed anything if I could. What to take from this is that you might have to compromise with courses, but in the end, they are all really good and it is good to try out something you may not have picked as your first priority. For me, however, three out of four of my courses would have been my first priority of I knew of them to begin with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for something that is not a part of your program, but still has a connection to your program! I chose a course in gender studies called 'queer and transgender studies,' which easily may be applied to cinema courses and the representation of queer and transgender people on the global screen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course levels are a little easier than those at the University of Copenhagen. The readings are the same level and difficulty, but more free creativity is included in assignments and finals. However, if you choose a course you have not had before, then maybe not choose a third-year course as that will be slightly difficult to follow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You have to engage in classes for grades, which is very different!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CIN340H1 - Special Topics in Cinema as a Social and Cultural Practice (overall topic: Film festivals)
CIN260H1 - Selected Topics in Cinema Studies (overall topic: The Global Romantic Comedy)
CIN380H1 - Global Screen Worlds
WGS376H1 - Studies in Queer and Trans

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ALL OF THEM! If you can find a course where Carrie Reese teaches, you should not question it. I had two courses with her, and she is a great and fun professor. Global Screen Worlds is always taught each semester, and it is very knowledgeable. I had fun with all my cinema courses and attended a lot of screenings as well. The course I had in Queer and Trans was as well very very giving and fun to engage in. You learn how to be critical of what you read and express your own opinion, which is very refreshing to include in academics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Toronto is a very expensive city and grocery shopping is expensive unless you do it in the right places! Phone bills are expensive as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and phone bills.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a free gym connected to the university! I attended pilates/cross-fit each morning with other people for free, and was very fond of it! Hart House has a lot of creativities included, which are very fun as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Fitness, music lessons, choir, group workout, film classes, running clubs, hockey, basketball, planting, yoga, etc. You can do everything you think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Barre! It is a group workout with an instructor that happens every Monday to Thursday morning/evening. It is 45 minutes of full-body workout sessions and so much fun (and tough).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Montréal and Vancouver, or rent a cabin out of the city and do some hiking! Explore the city because it has so much to offer! I always find myself wanting to try something new and I never feel like running out of stuff to do. Toronto has different neighborhoods such as Chinatown, Koreatown, Little Italy, Greektown, etc. There is a lot of nature in the area as well, which is easy to access.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Everyone is so friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Never be afraid to reach out or start talking to someone! Canadians are very friendly people and if you just walk up to someone and say hello, then you probably already made a friend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity. You find every culture in Toronto.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Don't expect that you can choose any course on the registration list! The only courses available can be found in the timetable.
2) Make sure to attend clubs and sports linked to the university, and also attend the university sports matches!
3) Choose one course that is not a part of your program at home. Something fun and different!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Libraries are free for students and cozy to study at.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from all over the world and finding a new home on the other side of the planet.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing social life and school. I cared about my courses because I liked them so much. But at the same time, I wanted to spend most of my time exploring the city - especially during exam periods.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Toronto if you consider it!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
